guide_enrichment.narrative:
For us, the case on Kansas starts with an offense our numbers expect to create scoring opportunities more consistently than Arizona State typically prevents them. Kansas’ opener against Long Island is not proof that the same production carries over, but 613 total yards and six plays of at least 20 yards showed that the rebuilt offense can generate both sustained drives and explosive gains. That combination matters when the market is asking Kansas to be treated as a more substantial underdog than our overall team ratings support.

We also see encouraging early context around Isaiah Marshall. In his second career start, he completed 14 of 19 passes for 246 yards and two touchdowns while adding 49 rushing yards, and the offensive line allowed no sacks and only one tackle for loss. The meaningful concern is on the other side: Arizona State’s passing offense gets a favorable efficiency matchup against a Kansas pass defense that rates poorly in our pass EPA numbers. We do not dismiss that path for Arizona State, but our view is that it is not enough to outweigh Kansas’ offensive ability at the available price.
guide_enrichment.matchup_to_watch: We are watching Kansas’ offense against Arizona State’s scoring-opportunity defense. Marshall’s mobility and the offensive line’s early protection give Kansas multiple ways to keep drives alive, while its downfield production creates a chance to score without requiring long, mistake-free possessions. If Kansas continues creating explosive plays while staying out of negative situations, that would support why our expectation is closer than the market’s.

recent_game.fact: Kansas opened the 2026 season with a 51-6 home win over Long Island on Sept. 4.
Kansas produced 613 total yards on 76 plays against Long Island, the eighth-highest single-game yardage total in program history.
Kansas rushed for 277 yards and five touchdowns against Long Island.
Kansas held Long Island to 146 total yards, 35 rushing yards on 33 attempts and no touchdowns.
Kansas recorded 11 tackles for loss and three sacks against Long Island.

opponent_notes.fact: Arizona State opened the 2026 season with a 70-7 win over Morgan State.
Arizona State is scheduled to play at Texas A&M on Sept. 12 before facing Kansas on Sept. 19.
Arizona State receiver Omarion Miller entered the week with consecutive 100-yard receiving games.

quarterback.fact: Kansas named redshirt sophomore Isaiah Marshall its starting quarterback before the 2026 season, replacing the role held by Jalon Daniels for much of the previous six seasons.
In his second career start, Marshall completed 14 of 19 passes for 246 yards and two touchdowns and rushed seven times for 49 yards against Long Island.
Backup Cole Ballard has played in 15 career games with one start and entered the season with 445 passing yards and three touchdowns.

Quarterback Chase Jenkins transferred from Rice after starting all 12 regular-season games there in 2025 and totaling 1,025 passing yards, nine passing touchdowns, 531 rushing yards and five rushing touchdowns.

offensive_personnel.fact: Kansas returned two 2025 offensive-line starters: left tackle Calvin Clements and left guard Amir Herring.
Kansas' offensive line allowed no sacks and only one tackle for loss against Long Island.
The Game 2 depth chart listed transfers Kasen Carpenter at center and Nick Morrow at right tackle, with Tavake Tuikolovatu at right guard.
Running back Yasin Willis transferred from Syracuse and rushed 11 times for 72 yards and two touchdowns in his Kansas debut.
Running back Dylan Edwards transferred to Kansas after two seasons at Kansas State and one at Colorado; he rushed six times for 32 yards in his Kansas debut.
Running back Jalen Dupree, a Colorado State transfer, rushed nine times for 35 yards and his first Kansas touchdown against Long Island.
Buffalo transfer Nik McMillan caught six passes for 130 yards and a touchdown in his Kansas debut, extending his streak to seven consecutive 100-yard receiving games.
Nahzae Cox recorded his first Kansas reception on a 47-yard pass from Isaiah Marshall against Long Island.

defensive_personnel.fact: Defensive end Leroy Harris III recorded a career-high four tackles for loss against Long Island after leading Kansas with 4.5 sacks in 2025.
Michigan State transfer David Santiago recorded four tackles, 1.5 tackles for loss, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery against Long Island.
Linebacker Trey Lathan returned after leading Kansas with 86 tackles in 2025; he entered 2026 with 198 career tackles and 17 tackles for loss.
Kansas added transfer linebackers Bam Crouch from Boston College, Quincy Davis from New Mexico State and Jibreel Al-Amin from Marshall.
Kansas returned cornerbacks Jalen Todd and Austin Alexander, who combined for 22 starts in 2025, and safety Taylor Davis, who started 10 games in 2025.
Kansas added experienced safeties Corey Gordon, who started 12 games for Louisville in 2025, and Jaden Harris, who previously started 13 games at Miami.

coaching_changes.fact: Andy Kotelnicki returned to Kansas as associate head coach after two seasons at Penn State; he previously served as Kansas' offensive coordinator from 2021 through 2023.
Kansas lists Jim Zebrowski as passing game coordinator and quarterbacks coach, Matt Lubick as co-offensive coordinator and tight ends coach, and D.K. McDonald as defensive coordinator.

injury_availability.fact: Wide receiver Cam Pickett, who tied for Kansas' team lead with 45 receptions in 2025, did not play in the 2026 season opener.
Boston College transfer linebacker Bam Crouch started four games in 2025 before missing the remainder of that season due to injury.

offensive_context.fact: Kansas had six plays of at least 20 yards, including three plays of at least 40 yards, against Long Island.
Kansas has averaged 19.7 yards per completion over the last two seasons, the highest figure in the Big 12 over that span.
Kansas has allowed 45 sacks since the start of the 2023 season, the eighth-fewest nationally and second-fewest in the Big 12 over that span.

defensive_context.fact: Kansas allowed 26.8 points and 387.2 yards per game in 2025 under defensive coordinator D.K. McDonald.
Kansas allowed 214.1 passing yards per game in 2025, its lowest season average since 2001.
Kansas averaged 6.3 tackles for loss per game in 2025, fourth in the Big 12.
Kansas has recorded 82 sacks since the start of the 2023 season.

special_teams.fact: Kansas added kicker Martin Connington from Michigan State, punter Matt Gill from Australia and long snapper Rino Monteforte from California for 2026.
Connington made a 32-yard field goal and all six extra-point attempts against Long Island.
The Game 2 depth chart listed Tate Nagy as the primary punt returner and Dylan Edwards as the primary kickoff returner.

series_context.fact: Arizona State leads the series with Kansas 1-0 after defeating the Jayhawks 35-31 in Tempe in 2024.

other_relevant.fact: Kansas and Arizona State are scheduled to play Sept. 19, 2026 at Wembley Stadium in London in each team's Big 12 opener.
The Kansas-Arizona State game is scheduled to be the first college football game played at Wembley Stadium and Kansas' first international game.
